page: Google Cloud Platform t2d-standard-1 is an entry-level general-purpose instance driven by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor using the x86_64 architecture. The server provides 1 dedicated physical core mapped directly to 1 vCPU with 1 thread per core, paired with 4.0 GB of memory. Cache capacity comprises 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. Supported instruction sets include AVX, AES, VAES, SHA-NI, BMI2, and FMA, whereas AVX-512 and AMX extensions are absent. The configuration does not include local disk storage or integrated GPU hardware, requiring network-attached block storage for persistence.

Benchmark evaluations indicate median-tier single-threaded performance contrasted with low total throughput due to the single-core constraint. In isolated processor tests, the instance records a Geekbench single-core score of 1484.0 and a stress-ng score of 2647.38. Data compression exhibits solid single-threaded throughput, reaching 25.79 GB/sec in gzip and 11.3 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. Aggregate multi-core metrics, such as PassMark CPU at 2226.38 and Geekbench multi-core at 1480.0, sit in the lower brackets because parallel execution is limited to one core. Uncached memory read bandwidth measures 21.24 GB/sec, while write operations achieve 18.37 GB/sec. Redis SET throughput measures 1.84 million operations per second, and static web serving achieves 1.73 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, t2d-standard-1 delivers predictable single-core performance without the CPU credits or variable throttling found in shared-core alternatives. The dedicated core eliminates hyperthreading resource contention, providing stable latency for modest workloads. The main operational tradeoffs are the absolute ceiling on concurrent computation and memory capacity, which preclude heavy parallel processing or large database deployments. The instance is suited for lightweight web serving, utility microservices, single-threaded batch tasks, and basic development or continuous integration runners.
description: Google Cloud Platform t2d-standard-1 is a general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 1 dedicated x86_64 vCPU derived from an AMD EPYC 7B13 physical core and paired with 4.0 GB of memory. The instance features a 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio and 32 MB of L3 cache, supporting standard instruction sets including AVX, AES, and SHA-NI, while omitting AVX-512, bundled local storage, and GPU acceleration. Benchmark profiles indicate solid median single-core compute performance, with Geekbench single-core reaching 1484.0 and stress-ng scoring 2647.38, alongside average compression execution. However, aggregate throughput, multi-core metrics, and uncached memory bandwidth remain constrained by the single-core ceiling. The dedicated core allocation ensures consistent compute delivery without the throttling risks associated with burstable instances. This hardware profile is appropriate for lightweight web serving, small background workers, automated testing runners, and low-traffic utility microservices.
